--- report head:
# OmniPaxos audit report

Source under audit: `work/` (mutable copy of `source/`, identified in the run brief as
`827f304846ab0c5aa40910b6f6cdce1d4ddf8e12`; `omnipaxos` v0.2.3 + `omnipaxos_runtime`
v0.1.0 + `omnipaxos_storage` + `omnipaxos_macros` + `omnipaxos_ui`).

Toolchain: `cargo 1.94.1` / `rustc 1.94.1`, offline. No source file of the captured
implementation was modified. All new files created by this audit are listed at the end.

## Executive summary

Three findings, each with a reproduction that another engineer can run. Two are deterministic;
the third is deterministic in its core shape and only shows up as an intermittent stall in the
captured suite.

| # | Where | Defect | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `omnipaxos_runtime/src/actor.rs` (`append_tracked`, `reconcile_unconfirmed`) | `append_notify` can resolve with the log index of a *different* entry — and before its own entry is even accepted. Requires `batch_size > 1` and a flush-triggering write followed by another buffered write in the same tick window. | 6 repro tests (2 also random-workload soak: 63–75 of 120 calls wrong), 2 controls pass; a candidate fix (queue a placeholder for the call's own advance) makes all 8 pass and leaves the captured runtime suite green (24/24) |
| 2 | `omnipaxos_runtime/src/actor.rs` (`DecidedSub::next_idx`, `push_to_sub`, `push_to_all_subs`) | A subscription starting below `compacted_idx` re-delivers the collapsed prefix item once per tick and re-delivers decided entries (cursor counts items, not log positions). Reachable by compacting the core instance before `spawn_actor`. | 2 repro tests: prefix delivered 6× (6 positions) and `Decided(104)/Decided(105)` delivered twice |
| 3 | `omnipaxos/src/sequence_paxos/{leader,follower}.rs` (`resend_messages_leader`, `resend_messages_follower`, `handle_sequence_num`) | A follower that misses an accept (and the decide that follows) is never brought up to date by the protocol itself: the leader re-sends no accepts despite tracking each follower's accepted index, the follower re-sends nothing in `Phase::Accept`, and `Outdated` messages are dropped silently. The StopSign `Decide` re-send reuses an already-consumed sequence number, so it can never take effect (source-confirmed, trace-observed). | 1 deterministic repro (follower stranded at `accepted = decided = 0` for 5000 rounds; one `reconnected(1)` fixes it), 4 probes pass, plus an instrumented stall trace of the captured `sync_full_test` |

Also recorded: negative results (the four `#[ignore]`d crash-recovery tests pass when run;
stale-leader adoption; a 4000-round partition/leader-churn safety soak; the StopSign
subscription boundary; `unicache` and workspace sweeps) and evidence-base caveats (two captured
runtime tests assert nothing; recovery tests are `#[ignore]`d; my first mechanism guess for
finding 3 was disproved by execution and is documented as such).

item.text:
This turn caught the decisive run and gave the report a proper front page.

**Role attribution settled for the stalled run.** With the diagnostic copy printing the test's own role line, a stall landed in run 4 of 6 under heavier load (`notes/diag_stall3_4.log`, 122.93 s): `follower_id=3 leader_id=2 nodes_to_stop=[1]`. So the node the test waits on *is* the reconnected follower (pid 3), the leader is pid 2, and the node stopped to block the write quorum is pid 1 — which rules out my earlier alternative reading ("the test may be waiting on the node it stopped") for that run, and leaves the leader-side picture: `decided_idx=9`, `accepted_indexes=[5, 9, 10]`, and its only outgoing traffic the StopSign `Decide` re-sent with `get_seq_num(follower)`.

**One inconsistency I could not close, reported rather than smoothed.** In that same run, the instrumented pid 3 prints `accepted=10 decided=9`, while the test's `read_decided_log()` on the same node returns a single `Snapshotted(trimmed_idx 5)` item — which by construction means `decided ≤ 5`. I named the two plausible reconciliations (a resync carrying a lower `decided_idx` than the node already had, since `sync_log` assigns it unconditionally; or my last per-pid print preceding the node's final transition) and left them as hypotheses, with the raw logs identified so the next pass can instrument the print site instead of the resend clocks.

**Report front page.** I added an executive summary table — finding, location, defect, and the evidence for each — plus a final verification table of all four audit test files, so a reader gets the result set and its provenance without reading 870 lines.

Current audit state: three findings (two runtime-layer with deterministic repros, one core liveness defect with a deterministic repro, a source-confirmed resend-arithmetic mechanism, and an instrumented stall trace), a substantial negative-result set, evidence-base caveats, a prioritised open list, and a full artifact inventory — [report.md](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-16_23-10-28-omnipaxos-baseline/work/report.md), four audit test files, three diagnostic copies (two instrumented), 57 logs under `work/notes/`.
